info.title: Ontosyx API
info.description:
The Semantic Orchestrator — Knowledge Graph Lifecycle Platform.

## Response envelope

Every successful 2xx response is wrapped in:

```json
{ "data": <T>, "pagination": {"next_cursor": "..."}?, "meta": {...}? }
```

Each handler's `responses(... body = T)` documents the type of `data`, **not** the wire shape. Generated clients should either unwrap `data` in a post-processing step (the approach `web/src/lib/api/client.ts` takes — frontend callers receive `T` directly) or wrap every response type in the envelope shape when consuming the spec from a third-party codegen.

Error responses use a separate envelope: `{ "error": { "type": "...", "message": "..." } }` (see the `ErrorResponse` schema).

allOf.description:
Kind-specific body. The `kind` tag + the variant's fields
appear flat at this struct's top level via `serde(flatten)`.

AdapterDetail.description:
Detail view of one registered adapter.

Wire shape matches [`RegisterAdapterRequest`] exactly, except
`credential` is the redacted [`CredentialSource`] instead of
the raw [`Credential`]. This symmetry means admin clients can
render the GET result with the same form UI that drives POST —
only the credential field needs a "re-enter inline value"
affordance (since the raw inline bytes are not echoed).

AdapterDetailKind.description:
Per-kind detail body. Mirrors [`RegisterAdapterKind`] with
[`CredentialSource`] in place of [`Credential`].

`schema_name` appears on the variants that actually use it —
`Option<String>` on `Postgres` (defaults to `"public"` at build
time), required `String` on `Mysql`, absent on the other three.
The old flat `Option<String>` field on `AdapterDetail` is gone;
csv / json / bigquery detail responses no longer carry a
nullable `schema_name: null` that meant nothing.

Adding a new adapter kind updates both this enum and
`RegisterAdapterKind`. The `From<&RegisterAdapterKind>`
conversion below uses an exhaustive `match` (no wildcard), so
forgetting the new arm surfaces as a compile error — the two
enums stay in lockstep.

ApprovalComment.description:
One entry in the comment thread attached to an approval. The
reviewer's decision-time rationale is the first comment; any
pre-/post-decision discussion follows in the same thread.

ApprovalRequest.description: Approval request — a queued gated operation awaiting review.

requester_name.description:
Display name resolved server-side from `users.name`. NULL when
the requester has been deleted from the workspace.

oneOf.description:
Apply immediately, no notification. For rollback + other
actions the system considers mechanical.

Apply immediately, broadcast a notification to the named
roles so stewards see the change in their feed.

Require approval, BUT skip the queue when any of the
predicates evaluate to `true`. The most expressive branch —
encodes "Admins sail through, high-scope edits get reviewed".

ApprovalRouting.description:
Destination for a classified change. Variants are ordered from
most-permissive to least so a reader can eyeball routing posture
without a legend.

oneOf.description:
The author's role matches or outranks this reference. The
named-field shape (rather than a tuple `AuthorHasRole(RoleRef)`)
keeps the wire JSON readable and compatible with serde's
`tag = "kind"` internal-tag discipline.

The op declares a scope of matching `scope` with a value
strictly under `threshold`. Ops that don't declare the
matching scope do NOT fire this predicate — "no scope"
is treated distinctly from "zero-sized scope" so an op
that never tracks its magnitude can't auto-skip by
accident.

ApprovalSkipPredicate.description:
Predicates the `ApprovalRequiredUnless` branch evaluates. Every
predicate returns a boolean; the skip list is OR'd (first firing
predicate short-circuits to Apply).

The predicate set is intentionally minimal — only signals the
routing pipeline can evaluate WITHOUT executing the edit. That's
why `HasValidationPass` is absent: under the
`route → apply → validate → commit` pipeline, the validate step
runs AFTER routing, so at decision time no validation result
exists. Every matrix row that conceptually reads "role X with a
passing validation" collapses cleanly to "role X" — the commit
path still requires validate to succeed, so a bad IR never lands
even when the role gate waves it through.

AuditRecord.description:
One record in the workspace-wide PROV-O audit stream. The
`provenance` payload is the content-addressed `ProvenanceDef`
emitted at IR commit time; the surrounding fields attribute it
to the source ontology.

AuditRecordPage.description:
Cursor-paginated audit page. The wire shape is
`{ items: [...], next_cursor?: string }`. `next_cursor` is
absent when no further pages exist.

ChangeRoutingRuleResponse.description:
Wire shape returned by the list / upsert endpoints. The
`change_type` round-trips through serde so the wire string
matches the storage format exactly (snake_case discriminator).
`routing` and `risk_level` come straight off the IR types —
no parallel schema, the FE consumes them through the
`OntologyEditOp` TS union alongside the rest of the matrix.

workspace_scoped.description:
`false` for global defaults, `true` for workspace overrides.
The UI uses this to badge override vs default rows.

ChangeType.description:
Taxonomy of edit operations the routing matrix knows about.
The variant set is closed — adding a new kind is a deliberate
schema extension, not a silent addition. Every `OntologyEditOp`
(Phase 2) classifies into exactly one of these.

model_override.description: Override the LLM model for this request (e.g., "claude-opus-4-6").

CreateOntologyRequest.description:
Request body for `POST /api/ontologies`.

`initial_operations` is optional — callers that only need the
shell (empty ontology with a pilot name) can omit it. When
present, the ops apply atomically: an error on any op or on the
post-batch `validate()` aborts the whole creation with nothing
persisted.

description.description:
Free-form description stored as the ontology's default
`LocalizedText`. Whitespace-only input collapses to the empty
localized text.

initial_operations.description:
Initial batch of edit operations applied atomically as v1.
Must contain at least one op — the handler rejects empty
batches with 400 so the endpoint stays symmetric with
`/edits`, which never accepts an empty operations list.
OpenAPI surfaces this as a free-form array — clients
discriminate on the internal `op` tag
(`create_glossary_term`, etc.) from [`OntologyEditOp`]'s
serde representation.

lineage_id.description:
Optional caller-supplied lineage id. When omitted a fresh
UUID seeds the lineage so cross-version references remain
stable across later refinements.

message.description:
Free-form commit message — surfaces in the version log next
to the first snapshot.

name.description:
Workspace-scoped name. Must be non-empty and unique within
the workspace (enforced by the store's `ontologies_ws_name_uq`
constraint).

CreateOntologyResponse.description:
Response body on successful creation. Carries enough data for
the FE to deep-link to the new ontology without a round-trip
refetch.

allOf.description: Project origin: source analysis or base ontology.

name.description: Unique name within (user, ontology) — UI uses it as a handle.

ontology_lineage_id.description:
Ontology the pattern was built against. The saved pattern is tied
to an ontology; reopening against a different ontology requires
the caller to decide how to reconcile unknown labels.

pattern_ir.description:
The full PatternIR — nodes with positions, edges, filters, and
layout hints (zoom + pan). QueryIR is computed on demand from
`pattern_ir.compile()` and does not need to be stored.

oneOf.description:
Raw value stored directly in the data_sources config JSONB.
The admin accepts responsibility for the confidentiality of
the persisted bytes (use `SecretRef` for credentials).

Opaque reference to an external secret store. The string's
scheme (e.g. `env:`) selects the [`SecretResolver`] branch
that dereferences it.

Credential.description:
Either a raw value or an opaque reference to a secret store.

The `value` field carries the raw value on `Inline` and the
reference string on `SecretRef`. A `SecretRef` is resolved at
adapter-build time through a [`SecretResolver`]; the resolver
dispatches on the reference's scheme prefix (`env:`, future
`vault:` / `aws-sm:` / `gcp-sm:`).

`Arc<str>` storage: see crate doc-comment — makes the inline
100 MiB CSV / JSON case zero-copy from request body to adapter.

oneOf.description: A raw value is stored; the raw value is NOT returned.

A reference string — safe to echo. `Arc<str>` to match
[`Credential::SecretRef`]; the view is built by cloning the
Arc (refcount bump), not by duplicating bytes.

CredentialSource.description:
Redacted view of a [`Credential`] for GET responses.

`Inline` credentials have their raw value stripped and reported
as a single discriminator — the admin API never echoes an inline
secret back out. `SecretRef`s carry only a reference string, so
we do echo those (operators need to see which env var their
registration points at).

cursor.description: Opaque cursor from a previous response's `next_cursor`

source_id.description:
Canonical source identity (`{source_type}:{fingerprint}`)
derived from `source_config` at project creation / reanalysis.

DesignProjectSummary.description: Design project summary (lightweight, for list endpoints).

ontology_id.description:
Optional saved-ontology id. When present, the OntologyValidator
gates the compiled Cypher against this ontology so a canvas built
on a stale schema gets rejected with a precise "unknown label"
error instead of a generic driver failure.

query_ir.description: The QueryIR to compile and execute.

compiled_query.description: The compiled query statement in the target language.

widget_hint.description: Widget hint for optimal result visualization.

data.description: Data batches to load. Each element is a JSON object representing one record.

ontology.description: OntologyIR for the target graph schema.

plan.description: Optional pre-computed load plan. If omitted, the plan is generated via LLM.

ontology.description: OntologyIR for the target graph schema.

source_description.description: Description of the data source for the LLM.

compiled_statements.description: Compiled statements in the target language.

ontology_ir.description:
Fully hydrated `OntologyIR` at the current version. `None` when the
identity exists but has no committed version yet — the caller
should treat it as an empty ontology (fresh project seed).

oneOf.description:
`None` iff the identity has no committed version yet — an ontology
can exist with no commits during multi-step create flows.

PageMeta.description:
Cursor-based pagination metadata.

Carries the opaque cursor used to fetch the next page of a
cursor-paginated list endpoint. Surfaces in OpenAPI under
`components.schemas.PageMeta`; list-handler responses include this
inside the universal `ApiResponse` envelope.

next_cursor.description: Opaque cursor for the next page. `None` when this is the last page.

query_ir.description: The lowered QueryIR, ready to execute via `/api/query/from-ir`.
The QueryIR to reconstruct onto the canvas.

editable.description:
`true` iff the source QueryIR was a `Match` operation and
therefore fully representable on the canvas. `false` for
PathFind / Union / Chain / Aggregate / CallSubquery / Mutate /
Analytics — the UI should surface a "read-only" indicator.

pattern_ir.description:
The reconstructed PatternIR. Positions are always `None` — the
UI runs its own layout pass before rendering.

PinboardItem.description: Pinboard item — a saved query result.

acknowledge_quality_risks.description:
Must be set to true if the quality report has low confidence or high-severity gaps.
Prevents accidental promotion of low-quality ontologies.

acknowledge_large_schema.description: Must be set to true if the schema has >100 tables and the user wants to proceed anyway.

dry_run.description: If true, returns generated commands without applying them.

user_request.description: Natural language description of the desired ontology change.

explanation.description: LLM explanation of what was changed and why.

source.description: New data source to merge into the project.

reconcile_report.description: Report on ID reconciliation between existing and new ontology entities.

base_ontology_id.description:
Identity of the ontology to seed the project from —
matches `ontologies.id`. The server resolves the current
version and hydrates its IR into the new project.

source.description: Data source to re-analyze (must match original source type).

invalidated_decisions.description: Design decisions that were invalidated by the schema change.

decisions.description: User accept/reject decisions for uncertain matches.

reconciled_ontology.description: Reconciled ontology with user decisions applied.

uncertain_matches.description: The uncertain matches being decided upon.

additional_context.description: Additional context for the LLM refinement.

reconcile_report.description: Report on ID reconciliation between original and refined ontology.

credentials_path.description:
Optional path to service account credentials JSON file.
Falls back to GOOGLE_APPLICATION_CREDENTIALS env var if omitted.

oneOf.description:
DuckDB in-process file analysis (Parquet, CSV, JSON).
The `file_path` must be an absolute path to a local file.

workspace_id.description:
When set, the prompt is a workspace-scoped override of the
global template. When `None`, it's a new global version.

PromptTemplateRow.description:
Prompt template row (admin-only — wired by `routes/prompts_admin.rs`).

`version` is the semver string (e.g. `1.2.3`). `workspace_id = null`
means the template is global; a concrete uuid scopes it to one
workspace (used by the `/api/admin/prompts` workspace-override flow).

code_system_json.description:
The full `CodeSystemDef` / `ValueSetDef` JSON — kept flat so
the admin UI can post them verbatim to `/edits` without
re-deriving ids.

oneOf.description:
Optional policy knobs. Defaults are tuned for high-precision
enum detection.

profile.description:
Profile snapshot (row counts + column stats). Wire-shape is
defined by `ox_core::source_schema::SourceProfile`.

schema.description:
Source schema snapshot — usually the `project.source_schema`
column of a design project, but any snapshot produced by the
introspection kernel is acceptable. Wire-shape is defined by
`ox_core::source_schema::SourceSchema`.

QueryExecutionSummary.description: Query execution summary (lightweight, for list endpoints).

ontology_id.description:
Optional saved-ontology id. When present, the runtime's
OntologyValidator gates the query against this ontology (rejects
unknown labels / relationship types / property keys). When
omitted, the raw path stays ontology-free and only the safety
+ workspace-scope gates apply.

query.description: Raw query statement in the target language (e.g., Cypher).

oneOf.description:
Register a CSV payload. Columns / types are inferred from the
header row; everything lives in one implicit `records`
relation (see `ox_source::sample::CsvAdapter`).

Register a JSON payload. Nested objects / arrays of objects
become child relations per `ox_source::sample::JsonAdapter`.

Register a PostgreSQL adapter. `schema_name` defaults to
`"public"` when omitted — matches the adapter's default.

Register a MySQL adapter. `schema_name` is *required* — MySQL
has no default-database equivalent of Postgres' `public`, so
the register call must name the target database up-front.

Register a BigQuery adapter. The connection string's own
`?credentials_path=...` carries BigQuery's auth path; no
`schema_name` because the dataset is already in the URI.

RegisterAdapterKind.description:
Adapter kind + its credential + any kind-specific options.

The outer `kind` tag on the wire is a `serde(tag)` discriminator,
so `{"kind": "csv", "credential": {...}}` matches `Csv`. Every
variant carries a [`Credential`]; a future `vault:` / `aws-sm:`
secret scheme is a resolver change, not an enum change.

allOf.description: Adapter kind + its credential + kind-specific options.

source_id.description:
Opaque identifier the planner looks up via
`ObjectMappingDef::source_id`. Stable — ontology authors
reference it by string in mappings.

RegisterAdapterRequest.description:
Request body for `POST /api/admin/federation/adapters`.

Wire shape:
```json
{
  "source_id": "sales_csv",
  "kind": "csv",
  "credential": { "kind": "inline", "value": "id,x\n1,2\n" }
}
```

`kind` is the outer tag; the body of each variant carries a
`Credential` plus adapter-specific options (schema name,
connection extras). The same struct deserialises both fresh API
requests and rows replayed from the `data_sources` table, so
register / preview / hydrate share the one source of truth.

adapter.description:
The inserted row, echoed so the client does not round-trip
its own input.

replaced.description:
`true` when a previous registration under the same `source_id`
was replaced. Useful so the admin UI can decide whether to
trigger downstream cache invalidation.

note.description:
Reviewer rationale recorded as the first comment on the
approval thread when non-empty after trimming.

RiskLevel.description:
Risk tier — metadata for UI badging and audit filtering. Does
not influence routing directly (that's `ApprovalRouting`'s job).

RoleRef.description:
Role reference. Declares the hierarchy at a symbolic level so the
routing rules don't hardcode workspace IDs.

ScopeKind.description:
Dimension a [`ApprovalSkipPredicate::ChangeScopeBelow`]
predicate measures against. Each op that cares about size
declares its own scope vector via
[`crate::OntologyEditOp::scopes`]; the predicate picks the entry
matching `kind` and compares its value against `threshold`.

New scope dimensions (table count, entity count, ...) slot in
as additional variants without changing the predicate shape or
breaking existing matrix rows / workspace overrides.

term.description: Canonical term name — the only required field.

term_id.description:
Pre-existing term id if the term is already saved. When
provided, the endpoint confirms it refers to the saved
definition; otherwise an ephemeral id is minted for scoring.

priority.description:
Priority — workspace overrides ship with `100` so they win
against the global `0`. Callers normally don't set this; we
default to `100` so a freshly-edited override clearly out-
ranks the seed row.

risk_level.description:
Risk badge surfaced in the admin UI; does not influence
routing directly (that's `routing`'s job).
